hook: The seller spent $12,000 on new gray paint and quartz countertops.
lines: The seller spent $12,000 on new gray paint and quartz countertops.

Then our two-inspector team arrived.
While my partner checked the electrical panel, I climbed into the attic.

Our FLIR thermal scan also caught an active water leak behind the master shower.
Repair estimate: $28,400.
The buyer got a $30,000 price reduction before 5:00 PM.
Fresh paint hides ugly secrets.
Hindsight is expensive... Choose Foresight.

hook: A solo inspector spent 45 minutes on a 4,000 sq ft home yesterday.
lines: A solo inspector spent 45 minutes on a 4,000 sq ft home yesterday.

The buyer called us because something felt off.

We also found a cracked heat exchanger leaking carbon monoxide.
A 45-minute inspection isn't an inspection.
It is an expensive game of Russian roulette with your family's savings.
Never let someone rush through the biggest purchase of your life.
Choose thoroughness over speed.

day: Wednesday - Deposit (The New Construction Shortcut Enemy)
hook: The site superintendent told my client: 'You don't need a third-party inspector.'
lines: The site superintendent told my client: 'You don't need an independent inspector.'
'The county building inspector already signed off on the framing.'
My client hired us anyway for a pre-drywall audit.
Within 10 minutes, we found three severed load-bearing roof trusses.
The HVAC contractor had cut right through them to run flex ducting.
The roof was literally sagging under its own weight before the drywall was even hung.
The builder had to halt the drywall crew and bring out a structural engineer.
County inspectors spend an average of 7 minutes on residential job sites.
They check compliance; we protect your equity.
Never close on new construction without an independent Certified Master Inspector.
Trust, but verify.

day: Thursday - Deposit (The Georgia Red Clay Enemy)
hook: Georgia red clay looks solid until it drinks 1,000 gallons of rain.
lines: Georgia red clay looks solid until it drinks 1,000 gallons of rain.
Then it acts like an expanding hydraulic jack against your basement walls.
Last week in Marietta, a buyer was told 'that small hairline crack is just settling.'
We put laser levels and digital moisture meters on the stem wall.
The foundation wall was deflecting inward by 1.75 inches.
Hydrostatic clay pressure had sheared the mortar joints below the grade.
Cost to install carbon fiber reinforcement straps: $16,500.
Hairline cracks are rarely 'just settling' in Atlanta's Piedmont soil.
Always measure the deflection before your due diligence expires.
Building science doesn't guess.

hook: The house was built in 2023 on a hill in Alpharetta.
lines: The house was built in 2023 on a hill in Alpharetta.
The buyer assumed high elevation meant zero environmental risk.
We placed our continuous electronic radon monitor in the basement for 48 hours.
The reading came back at 11.4 pCi/L.
The EPA action guideline is 4.0 pCi/L.
11.4 pCi/L is equivalent to smoking half a pack of cigarettes inside the home every day.
North Georgia sits on granite bedrock loaded with decaying uranium.
You cannot smell radon. You cannot see it. You cannot taste it.
The seller paid $1,800 to install an active sub-slab mitigation system before closing.
Never waive an environmental radon screen in North Metro Atlanta.

day: Tuesday - Deposit (The Missing Roof Flashing Enemy)
hook: The roof looked brand new from the driveway.
lines: The roof looked brand new from the driveway.
The inspector before us wrote: 'Roof inspected from ground level with binoculars.'
We don't use binoculars.
We launched our FAA-registered 4K drone over the two-story chimney.
The roofers had skipped counter-flashing entirely around the cricket.
They smeared black silicone caulk over open gaps instead of bending metal.
Rainwater was running straight down the chimney framing into the living room ceiling.
A $3,200 roofer shortcut caught in 3 minutes of 4K flight.
If your inspector doesn't walk the roof or fly a drone, you don't have a roof inspection.
High roofs require high standards.

hook: A brand new kitchen with designer matte black outlets.
lines: A brand new kitchen with designer matte black outlets.
Everything looked straight out of an Architectural Digest spread.
Then we plugged in our circuit tester.
Every single outlet along the island had an open ground.
The contractor had installed 3-prong receptacles onto 1960s ungrounded 2-wire cable.
Worse, he jumped the ground screw to the neutral terminal—a bootleg ground.
It tricks cheap plug-in testers into showing 'Correct Wiring.'
But if an appliance shorts out, the metal frame becomes energized at 120 volts.
It is an invisible shock hazard for anyone touching the sink and stove.
Never judge electrical safety by the color of the outlet cover.
Always verify with true digital metering.

hook: The toilets flushed perfectly during the open house.
lines: The toilets flushed perfectly during the open house.
The seller checked 'No Known Plumbing Defects' on the disclosure form.
We ran our self-leveling HD sewer camera 65 feet down the main lateral.
At 42 feet under the front yard, the old clay pipe was completely crushed.
Mature oak tree roots had invaded the bell joint and formed a solid wooden plug.
One week of regular household laundry would have flooded raw sewage across the basement.
Cost to excavate the front lawn and replace the sewer line: $9,200.
The seller credited the full $9,200 at closing.
A $250 sewer scope just paid for itself 36 times over.
You can't see underground without optics.
